title: Exact generic subrank in arbitrary tensor formats
formal: Historical question, resolved: for every algebraically closed field K, every tensor order k≥3 and all positive integers n₁,…,nₖ, determine the generic subrank Q_K(n₁,…,nₖ). Pielasa, Šafránek and Shatsila give the exact value min{n₁,…,nₖ,⌊(n₁+⋯+nₖ−(k−1))^{1/(k−1)}⌋}. Equivalently, it is the largest integer r≥1 satisfying r≤nᵢ for every i and r^{k−1}≤Σᵢnᵢ−(k−1). The formula includes both balanced and unbalanced formats.
context:
Applying one linear map to each tensor factor asks how many independent diagonal products can be obtained from the tensor. For three factors this corresponds to independent scalar multiplications embedded in a bilinear map.

Exceptional tensors can have a different subrank. The theorem identifies the value on a nonempty Zariski-open set of each ambient format, rather than bounding every tensor by that value.

The 2025 theorem covers arbitrary dimension tuples and all orders at least three. For three equally sized factors it reduces to Q_K(n,n,n)=⌊√(3n−2)⌋, and the same theorem answers the source’s separate higher-order/unbalanced question.

The original CCC paper assumes algebraic closure. A 2026 follow-up points out that the broader “any infinite field” wording in the exact-values paper needs this qualification. Retaining the original field assumption makes the resolution match the card without claiming a corresponding theorem for typical real tensors.
why: Determines exactly how many independent scalar products a generic tensor of any format can supply under linear restriction, completing a basic algebraic-complexity invariant.
status_note: Matched the CCC 2022 question and its field assumption to Theorem 3.7 of the 2025 published paper. sentences: Tensor subrank measures how many independent diagonal products can be extracted by linear maps on the factors.
Generic subrank is the value on a nonempty Zariski-open set of tensors of a fixed format.
The source asks for its exact value for all higher-order and unbalanced formats.
A 2025 published theorem gives the minimum of the factor dimensions and the rounded-down (k−1)st root of their sum minus k−1.
This resolves the original question over algebraically closed fields; a 2026 follow-up clarifies that field assumption.

references.title: Subrank and Optimal Reduction of Scalar Multiplications to Generic Tensors
references.authors: Derksen, Harm; Makam, Visu; Zuiddam, Jeroen
references.locator: Unresolved-question passage on page 21; PDF page 21

definitions: An algebraically closed field K is a field in which every nonconstant polynomial in one variable has a root. A tensor of format (n₁,…,nₖ) is an element T of K^{n₁}⊗⋯⊗K^{nₖ}, identified with its array of ∏ᵢnᵢ coefficients. For r≥1 let I_{r,k}=Σ_{j=1}^r e_j⊗⋯⊗e_j in (K^r)^{⊗k}, with k factors. The ordinary subrank Q_K(T) is the largest r for which there are K-linear maps Lᵢ:K^{nᵢ}→K^r satisfying (L₁⊗⋯⊗Lₖ)T=I_{r,k}; assign subrank zero to the zero tensor. The maps may be different in different factors and need not be invertible. A Zariski-closed set of tensors is a simultaneous zero set of polynomial equations in their coefficients, and a Zariski-open set is its complement. Generic subrank is the unique integer q such that Q_K(T)=q on some nonempty Zariski-open subset of the full tensor space. Such a subset exists in the source’s algebraically closed setting. The question concerns this generic value for each finite format, not the value on every tensor, the symmetric-tensor subspace, a limiting approximation to I_{r,k}, or tensor powers. All quantities and reductions are exact over K; no sampling distribution or numerical tolerance is used.
answer_criterion: The published formula supplies the requested exact value for every format in the original algebraically closed setting, with matching generic upper and lower bounds. A generic lower bound alone or asymptotic equality would not have sufficed. Results about border subrank, asymptotic subrank or typical real subrank are different targets.
